articles.title: Querétaro, Mexico’s Data Center Hub, Draws Projects Felt North of the Border
articles.narrative: Querétaro, Mexico, is rapidly emerging as a major data center hub, attracting significant investment and positioning itself as a key cloud region for Mexico and potentially the hemisphere. The state benefits from its strategic location, robust connectivity to the U.S., established industrial parks, and a favorable climate that reduces cooling costs. This growth is driven by increasing AI-driven demand for digital infrastructure, with developers finding Mexico a streamlined and cost-effective alternative to the U.S. market, which faces higher labor costs and community opposition.

people.name: John McWilliams
people.title: head of U.S. data center insights

people.name: André Rizzo
people.title: director of industrial, science and technology

articles.market_intelligence: Querétaro's geographical position between Mexico City, Monterrey, and Guadalajara provides desirable network latency. The state's mild climate allows data centers to operate with greater energy efficiency, reducing the need for constant chiller operation and mitigating some environmental concerns associated with data center energy and water consumption.

articles.title: Dolce & Gabbana Inks 21K-SF Office Lease at Feil’s 551 Fifth Avenue
articles.narrative: Luxury Italian fashion brand Dolce & Gabbana is relocating its New York City office headquarters to 551 Fifth Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, signing a long-term lease for 21,000 square feet. The move places the fashion house in a premier Midtown location, reflecting the landlord's strategy to attract a diverse mix of leading companies to the property. The building continues to evolve, drawing dynamic tenants seeking a prime Fifth Avenue address.

data_points.address: 551 Fifth Avenue, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Located at the corner of Fifth Avenue and 45th Street, three blocks north of the New York Public Library.

articles.title: Passion: The First Ingredient in the ‘DNA of Success’
articles.narrative: This opinion column argues that passion is the foundational element for achieving extraordinary success in commercial real estate and other fields. The author, drawing on over four decades of experience, posits that passion fuels discipline, curiosity, expertise, and personal growth, making the effort required for success feel less like a sacrifice and more like a privilege. He emphasizes that genuine passion is contagious, inspires others, and provides a durable foundation for sustained effort even through challenging market conditions, distinguishing it from temporary excitement.

articles.title: SASBs Dominate Conduits 3 to 1 in 2026 CMBS Market
articles.narrative: Single-asset, single-borrower (SASB) deals have dominated the private-label commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) market in 2026, accounting for 76% of issuance through September. This trend reflects a shift in capital allocation, with money rotating away from office and retail properties towards apartments, hotels, and data centers. While conduits continue to finance a broad range of smaller, everyday collateral, SASB deals are increasingly focused on trophy assets and large portfolios, with seven major banks originating the majority of this volume.
articles.market_intelligence: SASB deals accounted for 76% of 2026 private-label CMBS issuance through September, totaling $66 billion, compared to $21.2 billion for conduits. Combined volume of $87.2 billion is up 2% from the same period in 2025. SASB office volume fell to $12.5 billion from $22.4 billion a year earlier, and SASB retail halved to $5.1 billion. SASB multifamily rose to $10 billion (from $2.9 billion) and hotels to $11.3 billion (from $8.8 billion). Data centers reached $6.2 billion, comprising 9% of the SASB balance. Across both channels, multifamily's share more than doubled to 18% (from 8%), while retail fell to 9% (from 16%).

articles.title: Waste Storage Manufacturer Citibin Triples Footprint to 15K SF at Industry City
articles.narrative: Citibin, a manufacturer of waste storage enclosures, has significantly expanded its presence at Industry City in Brooklyn, tripling its warehouse and office footprint to 15,000 square feet. This five-year lease expansion was driven by increased demand for its products, largely due to New York City's new waste containerization policies. The company, which moved to Industry City in 2017, has consolidated its operations and grown its business to supply numerous business improvement districts and customers in other major cities.

data_points.notable_features: The space accommodates the manufacturer's inventory, installers, offices, and design teams under one roof.
data_points.project_notes: Citibin moved its operations to Industry City in 2017, consolidating from two warehouses in New Jersey and Brooklyn's Red Hook. The expansion was largely due to New York City's recent policies requiring waste to be stored in bins.

articles.market_intelligence: Asking rent for Industry City’s upper-floor industrial spaces range from $21 to $29 per square foot.

articles.title: JLL Negotiates Sale of 757,325 SF Industrial Park in North Houston
articles.narrative: JLL has negotiated the sale of Park 845 Crossing, a 757,325-square-foot industrial park in North Houston. The property, comprising five buildings, was sold by an affiliate of Equus Capital Partners to INDUS Realty Trust. The industrial park is strategically located at the interchange of I-45 and Beltway 8.

data_points.notable_features: Five buildings with rear-load and cross-dock configurations, 18- to 30-foot clear heights.

articles.title: Newmark Brokers Sale of 115,512 SF Shopping Center in West Austin
articles.narrative: Newmark has brokered the sale of Oak Hill Plaza, a 115,512-square-foot shopping center in West Austin. The property, situated on an 11.3-acre site, was 92.5 percent leased at the time of sale. Partners Real Estate, which had acquired the property in 2021, sold the asset to a joint venture between Trademark Property Co. and Cohen & Steers.

data_points.project_notes: Site previously acquired by seller in 2021.

articles.title: EōS Fitness to Open 40,000 SF Gym in Northwest Houston
articles.narrative: EōS Fitness will open a new 40,000-square-foot gym in northwest Houston, located at the intersection of Grand Parkway and State Highway 249. The new facility is expected to open next year, marking a significant expansion for the fitness chain in the area. NewQuest represented EōS Fitness in the lease negotiations.

articles.title: Cerenome Signs Life Sciences Lease Expansion in Houston
articles.narrative: Cerenome Inc. has expanded its life sciences lease at Levit Green, a 53-acre life sciences district in Houston. The company, which specializes in radiotherapeutics and diagnostic services for brain and central nervous system cancers, will now occupy 36,500 square feet of lab and office space. The expansion is expected to be completed by late next year, reflecting the growing demand for specialized facilities in the Texas Medical Center area.

data_points.notable_features: Located adjacent to Texas Medical Center.

articles.title: Alpine Residential Completes 500-Unit Multifamily Project in Jersey City
articles.narrative: Alpine Residential has completed AVIVA, a 500-unit multifamily project in Jersey City. The development consists of two 12-story buildings connected by a lobby base, offering a variety of floor plans and extensive amenities. Bank OZK provided the construction financing for the project.

data_points.notable_features: Two 12-story buildings connected by a lobby base, with ground-floor retail space and amenities including a fitness center, coworking space, and pet salon.

articles.title: Essex Realty Group closes sale of 12-unit multifamily building in Chicago’s Rogers Park neighborhood
articles.narrative: Essex Realty Group brokered the sale of a 12-unit multifamily apartment building located at 1706–1716 W. Farwell Avenue in Chicago's Rogers Park neighborhood. The property, which underwent a complete renovation in 2013, was acquired by a California-based 1031 exchange investor. The building features a mix of two-bedroom and three-bedroom duplex apartments with modern amenities.

data_points.notable_features: Completely renovated in 2013; features eight two-bedroom, two-bathroom apartments and four three-bedroom, three-bathroom duplex apartments; unit amenities include hardwood floors, granite countertops, stainless steel appliances, in-unit laundry, and individual tenant-paid HVAC. Located near public transportation and Loyola University Chicago.

articles.title: Gilbane Development breaks ground on Southern Gateway for Western Kentucky University
articles.narrative: Gilbane Development has broken ground on "The Southern Gateway," the initial phase of the $350 million "Elevate WKU" public-private partnership with Western Kentucky University. This multi-year initiative aims to modernize on-campus housing, replacing aging infrastructure with a student-centered residential experience. The first phase, scheduled to open in fall 2028, will deliver an approximately 1,000-bed residential community designed to foster connection and academic success for students.

data_points.notable_features: Designed to optimize the student experience with a mix of private and semi-private suite-style rooms, lounges, shared spaces, community kitchens, a 24-hour study area, new dining options, and a multipurpose classroom.
data_points.project_notes: This is the first phase of a broader housing transformation plan for Western Kentucky University, replacing Hugh Poland and Douglas Keen Halls.

articles.title: Crystal Lake Connects Growth and Investment to Build a Complete Community
articles.narrative: The city of Crystal Lake, Illinois, is strategically connecting residential and commercial growth with public spaces and transportation to foster a complete community. This approach is exemplified by the Water's Edge mixed-use redevelopment, which transformed a former shopping center into a vibrant destination with apartments, townhomes, retail, and public amenities adjacent to a major recreation area. The city is also revitalizing its downtown, focusing on small businesses and community activities, including the redevelopment of Depot Park. These efforts aim to enhance the resident and visitor experience by integrating new and existing assets, ensuring that housing, businesses, recreation, and transportation collectively strengthen the community's long-term economic vitality.

articles.title: Opportunity and uncertainty? That’s Pacer.ai’s outlook for the holiday shopping season
articles.narrative: Placer.ai's latest holiday retail research indicates that the 2026 holiday shopping season will be characterized by both opportunity and uncertainty, with forecasts for higher sales tempered by economic pressures influencing consumer spending and shopping locations. The analysis highlights a trend towards earlier big-ticket purchases, driven by October promotions, while traditional peak shopping days like Black Friday remain crucial for electronics and home furnishings. For smaller-ticket items, the opportunity shifts closer to Christmas, with affordable gifts expected to appeal to budget-conscious consumers. The report also suggests that shopping centers can capitalize on changing consumer behavior by offering dining, entertainment, and seasonal events to enhance the visitor experience and encourage longer dwell times.
articles.market_intelligence: Between 2019 and 2025, the share of October-through-December visits to electronics stores occurring before Thanksgiving week increased by 4 percentage points, and for home furnishings chains, that share climbed by 3.4 percentage points. From July to September, bookstores recorded the strongest year-over-year visit growth, followed by off-price apparel retailers and hobby, gift and craft stores. Visits to traditional apparel brands, department stores, and home furnishings chains fell year-over-year, while electronics stores saw a modest 0.4% increase.

articles.title: Partners Development breaks ground on 234,600-square-foot industrial park in Seguin
articles.narrative: Partners Development has broken ground on Seguin Commerce Park, an eight-building, 234,600-square-foot industrial development in Seguin, TX. The first phase, consisting of two 40,000-square-foot buildings, is slated for delivery in May 2027. The project is being marketed for sale or lease, capitalizing on Seguin's robust population growth and strong manufacturing employment base.

data_points.phase_1: Two 40,000-sq.-ft. buildings at 1781 and 1775 N Heideke Street
data_points.notable_features: Buildings range from 17,000 to 40,000 sq. ft. with 25-foot clear heights, crane-ready capability for some buildings, grade-level doors with dock-high well capability, 800-amp power, ESFR-ready sprinkler systems, and dedicated secured yards. Each building includes a 1,600-sq.-ft. finished office or build-to-suit option.
data_points.project_notes: The 20-acre site was previously acquired by Partners Development in February 2025.

articles.market_intelligence: Seguin's population grew 28.4% between 2020 and 2024, with nearly 18% of its workforce employed in manufacturing. Other industrial investments in the city include Ranch Hand's planned 400,000-sq.-ft. manufacturing facility and KTH Parts Industries' planned $127 million automotive manufacturing facility.

articles.title: Publix Building $200M Expansion at Lakeland Logistics Campus
articles.narrative: Publix Super Markets is undertaking a significant $200 million multi-phase expansion of its main distribution and logistics campus in West Lakeland, Florida. This investment will add a 400,000-square-foot warehouse distribution center and a 58,000-square-foot return center, solidifying Lakeland's role as the central supply chain hub for the grocer's extensive network across the Southeastern U.S.

data_points.project_notes: The 2.6-acre site was previously acquired in late 2023 for $8.25 million. The existing campus already spans over 1.1 million square feet.

articles.title: Camden County Looks to Redevelop 620-Acre Coastal Site
articles.narrative: The Camden County Joint Development Authority (JDA) has issued a Request for Proposals (RFP) seeking a national commercial real estate brokerage firm to advise on and market the future development of the former Gilman Paper Property. This 620-acre waterfront site in Camden County, Georgia, is slated for a comprehensive, phased mixed-use development that could include residential, commercial, recreational, and marina components. The JDA aims to attract a qualified master developer or capital partner capable of executing a large-scale, master-planned project that will provide long-term economic benefits to the county while upholding high standards of design and environmental stewardship.

data_points.notable_features: Waterfront site; former mill has been demolished and site cleaned up.

articles.title: Riverside Wharf JV Lands $145M Construction Loan for Dream Hotel
articles.narrative: A joint venture between Driftwood Capital, MV Real Estate Holdings, and Merrimac Ventures secured a $145 million construction loan from Centennial Bank for the Riverside Wharf project in Miami. This financing will facilitate the vertical construction of the $350 million hospitality-driven complex, which will feature a 167-key Dream Hotel, a large nightclub, event space, and signature restaurants. The development is expected to be completed in fall 2028.

data_points.address: 114 Southwest North River Drive, Miami, FL
data_points.notable_features: Includes a 30,000-square-foot nightclub, a rooftop pool day club, a 12,000-square-foot event hall, 16,000 square feet of restaurant space, a publicly accessible riverwalk, and a seawall.
data_points.project_notes: The development also includes the rebirth and expansion of The Wharf Miami and a pop-up location for Garcia’s Fish Market.

articles.title: Audi Building $4B Plant in C. Georgia
articles.narrative: Audi plans to invest approximately $4 billion to construct a new manufacturing plant at the Middle Georgia Megasite in Peach County, Georgia. This will be the first development at the 1,534-acre state-owned industrial site, which is strategically located near major transportation infrastructure and energy resources. The facility is projected to begin construction in 2027, with vehicle production commencing in the early 2030s, and is expected to create around 4,500 jobs, significantly boosting the regional economy and supply chain.

data_points.notable_features: Proximity to CSX rail, energy infrastructure, and Interstate 75; designed for automotive assembly and electric vehicle production with an annual capacity of up to 200,000 vehicles.
data_points.project_notes: The 1,534-acre site was previously acquired by the State of Georgia for approximately $18.6 million. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027.

articles.title: Tyler Henritze’s Town Lane Exceeds Target with $1.9-Billion Fundraise
articles.narrative: Town Lane, a real estate investment firm co-founded by Tyler Henritze, has successfully closed its second opportunistic fund, Town Lane Real Estate Opportunities Fund II, at its hard cap of $1.9 billion. This fundraise significantly exceeded its initial target of $1.5 billion and the $1.25 billion raised for its predecessor fund in 2024. The fund will pursue a flexible investment strategy across various commercial real estate sectors and capital structures in the U.S., focusing on themes with strong supply and demand fundamentals amid current market dislocations.

articles.title: AI Boom Keeps Data Center Supply Chains Stretched To The Breaking Point
articles.article_type: Market Research / Data Center Supply Chain
articles.narrative: The rapid expansion of the data center sector is encountering significant headwinds due to ongoing supply chain disruptions. These shortages are causing substantial delays in project timelines and driving up development costs, creating challenges for operators and developers aiming to meet the surging demand for data processing capacity, particularly from the artificial intelligence boom.

articles.title: BKM Capital Isn't Tapping The Brakes On Its $3B Industrial Buying Spree
articles.narrative: BKM Capital Partners, a California-based firm, has exceeded its annual acquisition target for light industrial real estate, demonstrating continued strong investment in the sector. The firm is actively pursuing further acquisitions as part of its ongoing strategy.

articles.title: One Week. 2 Schemes. More Than 2,000 London Homes Cancelled
articles.narrative: British Land has paused the second phase of its Canada Water development, citing escalating construction costs. This decision impacts the delivery of over 2,000 homes in London, highlighting the challenges developers face in the current economic climate.

data_points.project_notes: Development halted due to rising costs.

articles.title: Ireland's Top Resi Developers Plead For Stability After Regulation Roulette
articles.narrative: Ireland's leading real estate developers are advocating for a stable regulatory environment to encourage global investment, following a period marked by frequent policy changes. They argue that consistent regulations are crucial for long-term planning and attracting the necessary capital for large-scale residential projects.
